records.title: RAGForge: RAG & MCP Agent
records.description: A production-style AI knowledge platform that combines retrieval-augmented generation, semantic vector search, conversational memory, LLM agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools in a modular FastAPI backend.
records.technology: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, pgvector, Sentence Transformers, Google Gemini, Model Context Protocol (MCP), PyMuPDF / PyPDF, python-docx, Docker, Pytest, Render, Neon
records.tagline: Production-style RAG and agent platform with pgvector search, conversational memory and MCP tools on a FastAPI backend.
records.problem: LLMs on their own cannot answer from a team's private documents or remember earlier turns of a conversation, so answers are ungrounded and stateless.
records.solution: RAGForge ingests PDF, DOCX and TXT files, chunks and embeds them into PostgreSQL with pgvector, and exposes a Gemini-powered agent that discovers and calls MCP tools (document search, conversation history) to return grounded, session-aware answers. Key engineering highlights: Document ingestion pipeline for PDF, DOCX and TXT; Configurable text chunking (chunk size and overlap); Sentence-Transformer embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2); pgvector semantic search with configurable TOP_K and similarity threshold; Gemini-powered agent with dynamic MCP tool discovery and invocation (search_documents, get_conversation_history); Persistent chat sessions and multi-turn conversational memory in PostgreSQL; REST API with Swagger / OpenAPI documentation; Health checks for the API, database and LLM; Pytest suite, Docker support and structured request logging.
records.result_impact: Delivers grounded, session-aware answers over private PDF, DOCX and TXT documents through a REST API with Swagger docs, health checks, a Pytest suite and Docker support. A live API docs endpoint is available. Note: Hosted on Render's free tier; the first request after inactivity can be slow while the service wakes up.
records.arch_desc: Agent → MCP Client → MCP Server → Tools → Services, backed by PostgreSQL + pgvector. Inputs: User. Pipeline stages: Document Ingestion; Chunking. Services: FastAPI; MCP Client + Server; Vector Retrieval (search_documents). AI/ML components: Embeddings; Gemini Agent. Storage: PostgreSQL + pgvector; Conversation History. Outputs: Final Answer.

records.title: AI Customer Support Agent
records.description: End-to-end FastAPI agent platform with RAG, conversation memory, customer and order tools, a ticket API, escalation and audit records, packaged with Docker Compose.
records.technology: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, RAG, AI Agents, Docker, Pytest
records.tagline: FastAPI support agent with RAG, conversation memory, customer and order tools, ticketing, escalation and audit records.
records.problem: Support teams field repetitive customer and order questions and need answers grounded in knowledge-base content, with a clear path to a human when the agent cannot resolve an issue.
records.solution: A FastAPI agent answers from a knowledge base using RAG, keeps conversation memory, calls customer and order tools, raises tickets through an API and escalates with audit records. Key engineering highlights: RAG over knowledge-base content (lexical retrieval today); Conversation memory across turns; Customer and order lookup tools; Ticket API with escalation workflow; Audit records for agent actions; One-command Docker Compose setup with interactive /docs; Pytest test suite.
records.result_impact: Delivers a support agent that answers from a knowledge base, calls customer and order tools, raises tickets and escalates to a human with audit records, runnable with one Docker Compose command and covered by a Pytest suite. Planned next steps: Replace lexical retrieval with embeddings + pgvector hybrid search; Add explicit LangGraph state transitions; Add authentication and tracing; Add a labelled evaluation set.

records.title: QLoRA Heart Disease Predictor
records.description: Fine-tuning an LLM using QLoRA techniques for a healthcare prediction task, demonstrating parameter-efficient fine-tuning and practical LLM adaptation.
records.technology: Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face / Transformers, PEFT / QLoRA / TRL, BitsAndBytes, Scikit-learn, Pandas
records.tagline: Parameter-efficient QLoRA fine-tuning of an LLM to predict cardiovascular disease risk from patient records.
records.problem: Standard full-parameter fine-tuning of large language models for specialized healthcare prediction tasks is computationally prohibitive and memory-intensive on consumer GPU hardware.
records.solution: Adapts an open-weights causal language model using 4-bit NormalFloat quantization and Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA), enabling parameter-efficient fine-tuning on patient clinical records to predict cardiovascular disease risk. Key engineering highlights: 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization via BitsAndBytes to minimize VRAM usage during training; Parameter-efficient fine-tuning applying Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) target modules; Instruction-formatted prompt engineering wrapping tabular patient clinical attributes; Supervised fine-tuning execution leveraging gradient accumulation and mixed-precision arithmetic; Validation tracking using perplexity, evaluation loss, and ROC-AUC classification metrics.
records.result_impact: Enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning of an LLM on limited GPU memory, tracked with perplexity, evaluation loss and ROC-AUC, to predict cardiovascular disease risk. Published as a public Kaggle notebook.
records.arch_desc: Tabular Clinical Records → Instruction Formatter → 4-bit Quantized Base Model + LoRA Adapters → Fine-Tuned Prediction Output. Inputs: Clinical Patient Records. Pipeline stages: Instruction Formatter; SFT Trainer Pipeline. AI/ML components: 4-bit Quantized LLM (BitsAndBytes); PEFT LoRA Adapters. Outputs: Heart Disease Risk Prediction.

records.title: PDF Chatbot (Streamlit RAG)
records.description: Kaggle notebook prototyping a retrieval-augmented chatbot over PDF and document files with a Streamlit interface.
records.technology: Python, Streamlit, LangChain, Sentence Transformers, FAISS, PyMuPDF / PyPDF, Hugging Face / Transformers
records.tagline: RAG chatbot prototype that answers questions over uploaded PDFs through a Streamlit chat interface.
records.problem: Extracting targeted answers from custom PDF documents requires laborious manual reading, while generic LLMs cannot query unindexed user files.
records.solution: Implements an interactive document intelligence pipeline that ingests uploaded PDFs, indexes text chunks into a vector store, and streams grounded answers via a Streamlit web UI. Key engineering highlights: Multi-format document parsing supporting PDF and plain text input; Recursive character text splitting with configurable chunk sizing and overlap; Dense vector embedding generation using Sentence Transformers; Fast similarity search using an in-memory FAISS vector index; Interactive chat interface with session-state multi-turn memory management.
records.result_impact: Published as a public Kaggle notebook: an interactive Streamlit chat interface that streams grounded answers from uploaded PDFs with multi-turn memory.

records.title: Vortex Feature Diagnostics
records.description: A lightweight Python engine that bridges raw data and model-ready features: it detects data levels (nominal to ratio), runs statistical diagnostics, scores features with LightGBM and renders visual diagnostic grids in one line of code.
records.technology: Python, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, LightGBM, Matplotlib, Seaborn
records.tagline: One-line feature diagnostics: data-level detection, statistical checks and LightGBM signal scoring with visual grids.
records.problem: Judging which raw features carry real predictive signal usually means rewriting the same profiling and plotting code for every new dataset.
records.solution: One call classifies each feature's measurement level, reports skew, kurtosis and outliers, scores predictive strength with LightGBM gain and AUC-ROC, and labels features as Strong Signal or Global Noise, alongside auto-generated visual grids. Key engineering highlights: Smart data leveling: Nominal, Ordinal, Interval or Ratio; Statistical diagnostics: skew, kurtosis and outlier detection; Predictive scoring with LightGBM gain and AUC-ROC; Strong Signal vs Global Noise feature labelling; High-visibility console summary reports; Three-row visual grids: distribution, outliers/composition, target relationship; Installable straight from GitHub in Kaggle, Colab or Jupyter.

records.title: Quad-Tune: 4x Optuna Tuner
records.description: A parallel hyperparameter optimization framework using Optuna, designed to accelerate experimentation and model tuning through parallel execution.
records.technology: Python, Optuna, Joblib, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, Multiprocessing, Pandas, NumPy
records.tagline: Parallel Optuna hyperparameter search that speeds up tuning by up to 4x across CPU workers.
records.problem: Sequential hyperparameter tuning using Optuna on complex tree-based ensembles is time-prohibitive and frequently underutilizes available multi-core CPU architectures.
records.solution: Implements parallelized Optuna trial execution using multi-worker background processes with shared memory storage, accelerating hyperparameter search speeds up to 4x. Key engineering highlights: Parallel trial execution across CPU worker processes via Joblib/loky backends; Configurable objective functions for XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost models; SQLite-backed or memory-shared Optuna study storage for safe concurrent trial writes; Automated trial pruning with MedianPruner to terminate underperforming hyperparameter runs early; Optimization lifecycle visualization plots including parameter importances and optimization history.
records.result_impact: Accelerates hyperparameter search by up to 4x through parallel Optuna trials with shared study storage and median pruning. Published as a public Kaggle notebook.

records.title: Vortex KFold Engine
records.description: A high-performance cross-validation wrapper for robust model training and experiment tracking that automates K-Fold and uses Cloudpickle persistence to avoid redundant training sessions.
records.technology: Python, Scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy, Joblib, Cloudpickle
records.tagline: Scikit-learn-compatible K-Fold wrapper that persists fold models and out-of-fold predictions to avoid retraining.
records.problem: Long cross-validation runs are wasted whenever a notebook restarts or a session times out, because trained folds are lost.
records.solution: A scikit-learn-compatible estimator runs Stratified K-Fold (classification) or K-Fold (regression) in parallel, saves fold models and out-of-fold predictions with cloudpickle, and reloads them automatically when they already exist. Key engineering highlights: Dual task support: StratifiedKFold for classification, KFold for regression; Automatic detection and reload of saved model ensembles and OOF predictions; Parallel fold execution with joblib; Cloudpickle serialisation for custom classes and lambdas; Drop-in scikit-learn compatibility via BaseEstimator; Progress logging with final CV score (ROC-AUC or R2).
records.result_impact: Avoids redundant training: fold models and out-of-fold predictions are saved with cloudpickle and reloaded automatically after a restart, ending with a final CV score (ROC-AUC or R2).
records.arch_desc: Resume-aware, parallel cross-validation with persisted artifacts. Inputs: Training Data. Pipeline stages: Parallel K-Fold Training (joblib). Services: Artifact Check (.cloudpickle / .npy). Storage: Saved Fold Models + OOF Predictions. Outputs: CV Score + Predictions.

records.title: SafeStack: Crash-Safe Stacking
records.description: A production-grade stacking classifier built for stable ensemble workflows: a disk-persistent 'wave' architecture prevents memory exhaustion, resumes interrupted fits and survives library-version mismatches.
records.technology: Python, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, Pandas, NumPy, Joblib, Cloudpickle
records.tagline: Crash-safe stacking classifier that checkpoints out-of-fold predictions to disk and resumes interrupted fits.
records.problem: Large stacking ensembles often crash from memory exhaustion or interrupted long fits, losing hours of training.
records.solution: Training runs in disk-checkpointed waves: each expert's out-of-fold predictions are flushed to disk immediately, memory is released after every fold, and finished work is skipped on restart, with compatibility patches for serialisation across library versions. Key engineering highlights: Artifact persistence and check-pointing of OOF predictions and experts (joblib, cloudpickle); Automatic resume of interrupted training; Aggressive memory cleanup (gc.collect and explicit deletion) after each fold; loky parallelism with shared memory via /dev/shm; Compatibility patches for LabelEncoder and final estimators; Apache-2.0 licensed.
records.result_impact: Prevents memory exhaustion and lost training time in large stacking ensembles: out-of-fold predictions are flushed to disk and interrupted fits resume where they stopped. Apache-2.0 licensed.
records.arch_desc: Wave-based stacking with disk checkpoints. Inputs: Base Experts. Pipeline stages: Wave Loop (per fold); Meta-Feature Reassembly. AI/ML components: Final Estimator. Storage: OOF Predictions Flushed to Disk. Outputs: Predictions.

records.title: AutoML-Lite Classifier Suite
records.description: A framework that trains and evaluates 30+ classification models in one run (linear, tree, ensemble, SVM, neural network, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) while guarding RAM and runtime.
records.technology: Python, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Pandas, Joblib, Psutil, Multiprocessing
records.tagline: Trains and ranks 30+ classifiers in isolated, resource-guarded workers with a live validation leaderboard.
records.problem: Comparing dozens of candidate models by hand is slow, and one heavy model can crash the whole notebook.
records.solution: Each model runs in an isolated worker process with a 15-minute time limit and a 10 GB RAM guard, is saved as a metrics-named .joblib file, skipped on re-runs, and ranked in a live leaderboard by validation accuracy. Key engineering highlights: Catalog of 30+ classifiers including boosting, trees, ensembles, SVMs and neural networks; Active-kill resource guard (900 s time limit, 10 GB RAM threshold); Models persisted as .joblib files named with their metrics; Live leaderboard (score_df) sorted by validation accuracy; Smart resumption that skips already-evaluated models; Lifecycle helpers: inspect a model, clean up the directory, zip results.
records.result_impact: Evaluates 30+ classifiers in one run without crashing the notebook, using isolated workers with a 15-minute time limit and a 10 GB RAM guard, ranked in a live leaderboard by validation accuracy.
records.arch_desc: Isolated, resource-guarded model marathon. Inputs: Train / Validation Data. Pipeline stages: Model Catalog (30+). Services: Isolated Workers + Resource Guard. Storage: Saved .joblib Models. Outputs: Live Leaderboard.

records.title: Mission Control: Jupyter Job Monitor
records.description: A lightweight framework for launching long-running scripts (model training, ETL, Optuna tuning) as detached background processes, with a live external dashboard for logs and resource use that never blocks the notebook.
records.technology: Python, IPython, Jupyter / nbconvert
records.tagline: Runs long jobs as detached background processes from Jupyter with a live external log and resource monitor.
records.problem: Long training jobs inside notebooks block the UI, run into GIL limits and can take the whole session down when one process fails.
records.solution: Each task runs as an independent OS process tracked in a task registry, with logs streamed to an external monitor window and CPU-core usage reported on demand. Key engineering highlights: Detached execution that bypasses the GIL; Live external log monitor in its own browser window; Task registry that manages PIDs and restarts to avoid orphan processes; CPU core tracking: used, pending and total; Monitor window closes automatically when the engine stops; Hot-swap worker scripts without touching other tasks or notebook state.
records.result_impact: Keeps notebooks responsive during long training or ETL jobs: tasks run as independent OS processes with a live external monitor and CPU-core tracking.
records.arch_desc: Notebook-controlled detached workers with a live monitor. Inputs: Jupyter Notebook. Pipeline stages: Detached Worker Processes. Services: MissionControl Engine. Storage: Task Registry (PIDs). Outputs: Live External Monitor.

records.technology: Python, Scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, Pandas, NumPy
records.tagline: Drift-aware stacking ensemble with probability calibration to predict irrigation need.
records.problem: Agricultural irrigation requirement datasets exhibit severe concept drift and uncalibrated class probability estimates due to changing seasonal climate features.
records.solution: Key engineering highlights: Data drift detection and adaptive feature alignment across temporal training slices; Heterogeneous base ensemble integrating LightGBM, XGBoost, and CatBoost regressors/classifiers; Out-of-fold probability prediction generation via Stratified K-Fold cross-validation; Post-hoc model calibration using Isotonic Regression and CalibratedClassifierCV; Stacked meta-learner integration for refined decision boundaries.

records.title: Calibrated LightGBM Classifier
records.description: Combines custom feature engineering, Optuna-tuned LightGBM hyperparameter optimization, and probability calibration layers for enhanced log-loss evaluation. Built with Python, LightGBM, Scikit-learn, Optuna, Pandas and NumPy, and published as a public Kaggle notebook.
records.technology: Python, LightGBM, Scikit-learn, Optuna, Pandas, NumPy
records.tagline: Optuna-tuned, calibrated LightGBM pipeline with interaction features for better log-loss.
records.problem: Standard LightGBM gradient boosted trees frequently output overconfident probability scores under non-stationary or noise-corrupted feature distributions.
records.solution: Key engineering highlights: Automated domain-specific feature transformations and high-order interaction generation; Optuna Bayesian search for optimal LightGBM tree depth, learning rate, and regularization; Stratified K-Fold cross-validation scheme to prevent data leakage in out-of-fold predictions; Platt Scaling (Sigmoid) and Isotonic calibration layers for accurate risk probability output; Comprehensive validation tracking with ROC-AUC, Brier Score, and Log-Loss benchmarks.
records.result_impact: Published as a public Kaggle notebook producing calibrated class probabilities from an Optuna-tuned LightGBM for improved log-loss evaluation.

records.technology: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Requests, Jupyter / nbconvert, GitHub Actions, Kaggle API, IMF WEO API, World Bank API, FRED / FRED API
records.tagline: Weekly auto-updated country-year panel of sovereign debt and crisis-risk signals for ~180 countries, from IMF, World Bank and FRED data.
records.problem: Sovereign-debt indicators are scattered across IMF, World Bank and FRED sources in different formats, which makes crisis-risk analysis and model training slow to set up.
records.solution: A notebook pipeline merges the sources into one country-year panel with a composite 0-100 debt-crisis risk score and an ML-ready feature matrix, and GitHub Actions refreshes and republishes it to Kaggle every week. Key engineering highlights: Merged panel for ~180 countries covering debt burden, fiscal health and risk signals; Composite 0-100 risk score: 40% debt/GDP, 30% interest/revenue, 30% inverse reserves-to-external-debt; ML feature matrix with lags, rolling windows and year-over-year changes, computed without leakage; Weekly automated refresh through GitHub Actions; Automatic publishing to Kaggle via the Kaggle API; Free, open data sources (only a free FRED key needed).

records.description: An auto-updating pipeline that fetches, merges and publishes a monthly food-security panel (FAO Food Price Index, World Bank commodity and fertiliser prices, crop yields and ML-ready features) to Kaggle every Monday.
records.technology: Python, Pandas, NumPy, curl_cffi, OpenPyXL, Jupyter / nbconvert, GitHub Actions, Kaggle API, FAO FAOSTAT, World Bank API
records.tagline: Auto-updating food-security pipeline that merges FAO and World Bank data into a monthly panel published to Kaggle.
records.problem: Food-price, fertiliser, crop-yield and food-security data live in separate sources, and keeping a merged, current dataset by hand is tedious.
records.solution: A GitHub Actions workflow runs a notebook every Monday that pulls live FAO and World Bank data, writes six cleaned CSVs and pushes a new version to Kaggle, with a fallback chain so output is always produced. Key engineering highlights: Six output files: FAO price indices, commodity prices, crop yields, food-security indicators, merged panel and ML features; Six derived food-security ratios such as cereals affordability and DAP-to-wheat ratio; Crisis and supply-stress flags plus ML targets for regression and classification; Resilient fallback chain: FAOSTAT ZIP, FAOSTAT REST API, then a proxy built from World Bank Pink Sheet prices; Weekly automation (Monday 07:00 UTC) with no manual steps after setup; Code under MIT licence, source data open-access.
records.result_impact: Produces six cleaned CSVs from FAO and World Bank data and publishes a new Kaggle version every Monday, with a fallback chain so output is always produced and no manual steps after setup. records.title: Retail Demand Forecasting
records.description: Applies time-series forecasting models to historical retail sales data to predict SKU demand and optimize reorder stock levels. Built with Python, Pandas, Statsmodels, Scikit-learn and Matplotlib, and completed as a Skill-Lync course project.
records.technology: Python, Pandas, Statsmodels, Scikit-learn, Matplotlib
records.tagline: Time-series demand forecasting to set SKU reorder points and reduce stockouts and overstock.
records.problem: Retail store networks suffer stockout losses and overstock holding costs due to imprecise SKU-level demand forecasts.
records.solution: Key engineering highlights: Time-series decomposition identifying sales trend, seasonality, and residual noise; ARIMA and Holt-Winters exponential smoothing demand forecasting models; Safety stock and optimal reorder point (ROP) calculation per SKU; Stockout risk evaluation comparing forecasted demand against current stock levels; Visual forecasting comparison plots and inventory optimization outputs.
records.result_impact: Completed as a Skill-Lync course project; final output: Inventory Reorder Schedule Output.

records.title: Patient Readmission Predictor
records.description: Develops a machine learning classification model predicting 30-day diabetic patient readmission risk using electronic health records. Built with Python, Scikit-learn, Pandas, Logistic Regression and Random Forest, and completed as a Skill-Lync course project.
records.technology: Python, Scikit-learn, Pandas, Logistic Regression, Random Forest
records.tagline: Machine learning model predicting 30-day diabetic patient readmission risk from health records.
records.problem: Hospitals incur severe financial penalties when diabetic patients are readmitted within 30 days of discharge without early intervention.
records.solution: Key engineering highlights: Preprocessing pipeline encoding clinical diagnostic codes, medication counts, and lab results; Class imbalance mitigation using Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE); Model training evaluating Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting; Feature importance scoring highlighting top clinical risk drivers (e.g., number of inpatient visits); ROC-AUC and Confusion Matrix evaluation metrics detailing model sensitivity.
records.result_impact: Completed as a Skill-Lync course project; final output: 30-Day Readmission Risk Output.

records.title: Credit Card Fraud Detector
records.description: Builds an imbalanced machine learning classification pipeline utilizing XGBoost to flag fraudulent credit card transactions in real time. Built with Python, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, Pandas and NumPy, and completed as a Skill-Lync course project.
records.technology: Python, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, Pandas, NumPy
records.tagline: XGBoost pipeline that flags fraudulent credit card transactions despite extreme class imbalance.
records.problem: Credit card fraud detection systems face severe class imbalance where fraudulent transactions represent a tiny fraction of total transactions.
records.solution: Key engineering highlights: Feature scaling and PCA component transformation on transaction amounts; Handling extreme class imbalance using SMOTE and Random Under-sampling; XGBoost classification model trained for high Precision-Recall AUC; Decision threshold tuning minimizing false negative transaction authorizations; Comprehensive model evaluation report detailing Precision, Recall, and F1-score.
records.result_impact: Completed as a Skill-Lync course project; final output: Fraud Detection Alert Output.

records.title: AegisAI: Production AI Agent
records.description: A production-oriented AI platform featuring a central Main Agent orchestrator, Advanced RAG with pgvector, MCP tools, asynchronous background worker processing, agent memory, clarification workflows, and security guardrails.
records.technology: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, pgvector, Google Gemini, Model Context Protocol (MCP), Upstash Redis, PyMuPDF / PyPDF, Docker, Pytest, Render, Neon, Tavily
records.tagline: Production-oriented AI platform with a Main Agent orchestrator, hybrid RAG, MCP tools, async worker and guardrails.
records.problem: Monolithic AI applications encounter high API compute latency during heavy document processing, lack controlled tool boundaries for agentic execution, and risk ungrounded responses when user context is incomplete.
records.solution: AegisAI implements a central Main Agent orchestrator paired with an asynchronous job system (Upstash + Voroa worker) for document ingestion, a pgvector-backed hybrid search RAG pipeline, controlled MCP tool interfaces, and automated clarification workflows. Key engineering highlights: Main Agent orchestration coordinating reasoning, memory, tools, and response generation; Hybrid search RAG combining semantic vector retrieval and keyword/context retrieval via pgvector; Controlled MCP tool boundary exposing hybrid_search, get_chat_history, get_memories, and search_web; Asynchronous document ingestion pipeline using Upstash Redis queues and Voroa background workers; Interactive clarification workflow replacing human-in-the-loop approvals when context is missing; Persistent multi-turn chat sessions and agent memory stored in Neon PostgreSQL; Application-level guardrails including upload validation, file size, agent step, tool call, and time limits; CI/CD setup with GitHub Actions running Pytest, Alembic migrations, and pgvector against temporary DBs.
records.result_impact: Delivers a deployed AI platform: a Main Agent orchestrates reasoning, memory, tools and responses; document ingestion runs asynchronously on Upstash queues with a Voroa worker; application-level guardrails and a CI/CD pipeline running Pytest cover the stack. A live API docs endpoint is available. Note: API hosted on Render free tier; background worker deployed on Voroa. Planned next steps: Add dynamic web UI for administration and memory management; Implement automated evaluation and threat scoring benchmarks.
records.arch_desc: Client → Render (FastAPI) → Main Agent → MCP Tools / Neon PostgreSQL + pgvector / Gemini LLM → Upstash Redis Queue → Voroa Background Worker. Inputs: Client. Services: Render (FastAPI API); MCP Tools (Retrieval, Memory, Search); Voroa Background Worker. AI/ML components: Main Agent Orchestrator; Gemini LLM & Embeddings. Storage: Neon PostgreSQL + pgvector; Upstash Redis Queue/Cache.
